column1: # Declared boundary cases for the models hierarchy (run A).
# Every row is a case the rules of MODELS_DERIVATION_BRIEF section 4 do not
# decide cleanly. The reading CHOSEN and the reading REJECTED are both recorded,
# so that overruling any row is a one-line change rather than a re-derivation.
# None of these was resolved silently, and none was resolved by the corpus.
# Columns: case_id, subject, rule_in_tension, reading_chosen, reading_rejected,

column2: subject
column4: reading_chosen
column5: reading_rejected
column6: why
column7: consequence

column2: vit / conformer: placed under `Encoder-only Transformer', not directly under `transformer'
column3: R4 vs the brief's section 4.7 worked table
column4: ViT, Conformer, wav2vec 2.0, Perceiver, ESM and AlphaFold are children of `Encoder-only Transformer'
column5: The brief's own row: `vision transformer (vit) -> node under transformer'
column6: A division must be total over its parent's extension. Leaving ViT beside the three division nodes makes `Encoder-only' a non-exhaustive sibling of an artifact -- v0's exact defect, where `bert' sat among 95 flat leaves. ViT is unambiguously encoder-only.
column7: If the owner prefers the brief's literal reading, move ViT/Conformer/wav2vec2/Perceiver/ESM/AlphaFold up one level; nothing else changes.

column2: Generation series: GPT-2/3/4 are siblings under GPT, not a chain
column4: All generations of a series attach to the series' founding node; the predecessor is recorded in `notes'
column5: A strict R1 chain gpt -> gpt-2 -> gpt-3 -> gpt-4 (GPT-3's paper: `same model and architecture as GPT-2')
column6: A chain pushes designed depth to 5-6 in the largest families and makes the usable cut depend on generation number. The brief's section 3 diagram flattens exactly this way.
column7: Generation order survives only in `notes', so a query like `what descends from GPT-2' cannot be answered from edges.

column2: `diffusion model' / DDPM / flow matching as bare terms
column4: Algorithm: the model is the denoiser (a U-Net or a DiT). Named systems (Stable Diffusion, Imagen, DALL-E 2) are composite nodes
column5: A `Diffusion model' node under which every diffusion system hangs
column6: The brief's own table assigns the model role to the denoiser. The denoising procedure is the contribution, exactly as for SimCLR.
column7: This is the largest single routing consequence in the corpus: `diffusion'-shaped strings are one of the two biggest clusters. If the owner wants a diffusion cut, it must come from the algorithms hierarchy or from a run-level field.

column2: CycleGAN admitted as a model, WGAN not
column4: CycleGAN is a node (two generators and two discriminators wired in a cycle = structure); WGAN is an algorithm (same architecture, different objective)
column5: Both as nodes, or both as algorithms
column6: The SimCLR precedent routes objective-only contributions to algorithms. The cycle wiring is structural; the Wasserstein critic is not.
column7: The line is thin and the second pass will meet many `X-GAN' names that sit on it.

column2: `energy-based model' as a bare term
column3: R6, and my phase-1 decision to drop an `Energy-based network' root
column4: Quarantined as a class generic; its named members (Hopfield, Boltzmann machine, RBM) are nodes under `Undirected graphical model'
column5: An `Energy-based model' root
column6: Energy is a cross-cutting property, not a lineage; a root for it would be a fifth way of saying `has an energy function'.
column7: The corpus contains the bare term, so those mentions produce no model. Reported as a finding, NOT as a reason to restructure.

column2: Mixture of experts
column3: Section 3 (a primitive is a property of a layer)
column4: Not a node: a property recorded in `notes' on the model that uses it (Mixtral, Switch)
column5: An `MoE' grouping node under Decoder-only Transformer
column6: Sparse routing is a feed-forward-block property; the same argument that rejected `computational primitive' as a level-1 characteristic applies one level down.
column7: `mixture of experts' as a bare corpus string resolves to nothing.

column2: Retrieval-augmented models (REALM, RAG, Atlas, FiD, kNN-LM)
column3: R4 (a grouping node must sit under one parent)
column4: No grouping node; each named system attaches to its parts as an R5 composite
column5: A `Retrieval-augmented model' node
column6: Retrieval augmentation cuts across encoder-only and decoder-only parents, so it cannot sit at one place in a lineage tree.
column7: The cluster stays invisible as a cut; it is recoverable only by listing the composites.

column2: Deep ensembles, MC-dropout, Siamese/two-tower wiring, prototypical networks
column4: Not nodes: the model is the base architecture; the wrapper is a run property or an algorithm
column5: Nodes for each
column6: N copies of one architecture do not change the learned object's kind; the compute multiplier belongs on the run.
column7: `siamese network' and `prototypical networks' appear in the corpus and will resolve to nothing.

column2: Bayesian neural network admitted as a node under MLP
column3: Admission rule vs the same wrapper argument as B08
column4: A node: the weights themselves are random variables, so `parameter_count' changes meaning
column5: A cross-cutting property like `energy-based' (B05)
column6: Unlike a deep ensemble, a BNN changes the parameterisation of a single network. The MLP parent is the canonical instantiation only -- a Bayesian U-Net is the same property elsewhere.
column7: The weakest of the phase-2 additions; I would not defend the MLP edge hard.

column2: PCA, CCA, LDA, Cox, naive Bayes, ARIMA, GLM: placed by kind, not by derivation
column4: Edges admitted on the shared defining idea (`the learned object is an affine map', `a directed factorisation')
column5: Leaving them unplaced because no paper frames them as derived from a parent
column6: R1's framing test presupposes a paper-derivation culture that pre-1990 statistics does not have. Refusing the edge would strand every classical model, and R7 forbids the second pass from inventing a parent.
column7: A declared strain: these edges are weaker evidence than, say, RoBERTa -> BERT, and the tree does not mark the difference.

column2: GLM is a child of Linear model although it CONTAINS it in extension
column4: Lineage wins: GLM was derived by generalising the linear model (1972)
column5: GLM as the parent of linear and logistic regression
column6: The backbone is `the child was derived from the parent' (section 3). Same shape for `Tree ensemble' under `Decision tree' and `MPNN' over GCN/GAT.
column7: The tree must not be read as an is-a taxonomy; an ancestor's extension does not always contain its descendants'.

column2: GRU is not a child of LSTM
column4: Parent is `Recurrent network'; the LSTM relation is recorded in `notes' as influence
column5: GRU -> LSTM, since Cho et al. frame the unit relative to the LSTM
column6: `Motivated by the LSTM unit but much simpler' reads as influence, and R2 names `inspired by' as the thing that would make the DAG complete and meaningless.
column7: If this is wrong, the same reasoning may be under-connecting other `simplified X' models.

column2: DenseNet, YOLO, 3D Gaussian splatting, DiT, Transformer: parents assigned by contrast-is-not-descent
column4: A paper that names an architecture in order to REPLACE it gets no edge to it
column5: Edges DenseNet -> ResNet, YOLO -> R-CNN, 3DGS -> NeRF, DiT -> U-Net, Transformer -> RNN
column6: `Dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely' is the clearest case; treating contrast as descent would make the Transformer a child of the RNN.
column7: It is the single reading that most shapes the root set; if the owner reads contrast as descent, the root set shrinks sharply and 3D Gaussian splatting stops being a root.

column2: MLP is a root, not a child of Perceptron or Linear model
column4: Root: the connectionist framing is not `a modified linear regression'
column5: MLP -> Perceptron -> Linear model
column6: The edge would make almost every network a Linear-model descendant, so `proportion of papers using a linear model' would stop meaning anything.
column7: `perceptron' and `multi-layer perceptron' share a word but not an edge, which will look like an error to a reader.

column2: GNN is a root, not a child of CNN
column3: R2 (shared primitive is never an edge)
column4: Root
column5: GNN -> CNN, since spectral GNNs are framed as generalising convolution to graphs
column6: What is generalised is the convolution PRIMITIVE, and R2 forbids primitive edges. The original (Scarselli) GNN predates and does not build on convnets.
column7: If the owner reads the spectral framing as descent, GNN becomes a CNN subtree and the `proportion using a CNN' cut swallows all graph work.

column2: No spectral/spatial division under GNN
column4: No grouping node; GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, GIN, MPNN are flat under GNN
column5: `Spectral GNN' / `Spatial (message-passing) GNN'
column6: Field-named and nearly admitted, but GCN -- the largest member -- is the bridge case (a first-order approximation of a spectral filter, universally implemented as message passing), so the division would misplace its biggest member.
column7: GNN stays flat and wide; flagged for a deeper design pass.

column2: No division under BERT
column4: BERT's variants stay flat, and the family is flagged for a deeper design pass
column5: `objective variants' / `corpus variants' / `compressed variants' / `multilingual variants'
column6: The four values do not partition: DeBERTa changes architecture AND objective, TinyBERT is compressed AND re-distilled, XLM-R is RoBERTa's objective on a new corpus. A division with overlapping values produces `X and Y' nodes.
column7: R7 means a flat BERT stays flat until a design pass runs. This is the brief's named example and the highest-priority follow-up.

column2: No 1-D / 2-D / 3-D division under CNN
column3: Section 3 (data structure consumed is a property of the application)
column4: No grouping node; TCN, WaveNet, I3D attach flat
column5: `Temporal convnet' / `Spatial convnet' / `Spatiotemporal convnet'
column6: This is the least clearly wrong of the three rejected level-1 characteristics -- kernel rank really is fixed in the weights -- but it is still the rejected characteristic, applied one level down.
column7: Recorded so the owner can overrule it; it is the one rejected division I would most readily revisit.

column2: Neural process: two parents, one of them weak
column4: Parents {Deep Sets, Gaussian process}
column5: Gaussian process alone, or Deep Sets alone
column6: The permutation-invariant context aggregation is a genuine structural inheritance; the GP edge records what the family amortises and is closer to R2 influence.
column7: If the GP edge is refused, neural processes sit purely under Deep Sets and the kernel-machine cut loses them.

column2: Slot attention admitted as a root
column4: Root: competition over slots plus a recurrent update is a new founding idea
column5: A child of Transformer, since the paper defines its attention by swapping the softmax axis of standard dot-product attention
column6: The swapped normalisation is a redefinition of the mechanism, not a modification of the Transformer block, and slot attention fits none of the three stack divisions.
column7: A root with one real member, added in phase 2; the same smell as 3D Gaussian splatting.

column2: PointNet under Deep Sets
column4: Parent Deep Sets
column5: Parent CNN, or a root
column6: Both are 2017 and the construction (per-element MLP + symmetric pooling) is shared; the edge leans on shared construction, which is close to an R2 similarity edge.
column7: One of the few edges in the tree I would call a reconstruction rather than a framing.

column2: `lda' is not resolved
column4: The bare acronym resolves to NOTHING: it is ambiguous between latent Dirichlet allocation and linear discriminant analysis
column5: Resolving it to whichever is more frequent
column6: Both are in the corpus, both are models, and they sit in different roots. An automatic collapse would silently merge two families.
column7: Other collisions found: `dino' (objective vs released backbone), `sam' (Segment Anything vs the SAM optimiser), `complex' (ComplEx vs the English word), `ar' / `art' / `ego' / `goat' / `clean'.

column2: Product names: ChatGPT, Copilot, Bard, Midjourney
column4: A product name is a NODE under the family whose release it serves (ChatGPT under GPT; Copilot under Codex), when the vendor states the lineage
column5: Treating ChatGPT as a spelling of GPT-3.5/GPT-4
column6: The served model changes over time, so a product is not `the same release under a different string'. But Midjourney has no published lineage and is UNPLACEABLE: R7 forbids the second pass from inventing a parent.
column7: Policy needed: unplaceable closed products must be flagged for a design pass, not guessed.

column2: `models[]' contains out-of-type terms
column4: Three declared out-of-type classes, quarantined and reported separately from generics: (a) libraries and tools -- pytorch, gurobi, core ml, google translate; (b) mechanistic/domain models -- epidemiological compartmental models, cold dark matter, mouse models, ball-and-stick models; (c) metrics and procedures -- FID, Elo, t-SNE, backpropagation, Gibbs sampling
column5: Forcing them into the tree, or treating them as generics
column6: They are not uninformative names for models; they are names for things that are not models. Conflating them with `neural network' would hide an extraction defect.
column7: Family shares must exclude all three classes separately, and class (a) duplicates the libraries[] contamination noted in MODELS_BRIEF Part C.

column2: MuZero, AlphaZero, Dreamer
column4: Algorithms; the model entity is the learned dynamics network (RSSM for Dreamer/PlaNet)
column5: Nodes under a `world model' family
column6: Consistent with PPO/SAC/DQN in the brief's own table: the update rule is the algorithm and the networks are the models.
column7: `muzero', `dreamerv2' and friends are frequent in this corpus and will produce an algorithm with no named model unless the paper names the network.

column2: nnU-Net
column4: A node under U-Net
column5: An algorithm: its contribution is a self-configuration procedure, not an architecture
column6: It is named, released and run as a model, and the configured object is a U-Net.
column7: If refused, several `pipeline-shaped' names (AutoML systems, configured segmentation tools) lose their only home.

column2: XGBoost, LightGBM: model or library
column4: Nodes in the models tree; the library sense belongs in libraries[]
column5: A library only
column6: The brief's own table admits XGBoost as `a gradient-boosted tree ensemble'.
column7: The same string will appear in both dimensions, which is correct but must not be read as duplication.

column2: SE-ResNet / SENet, FPN, Slot attention, Highway: component vs model
column4: Admitted as nodes where the component is separately named, released and run (SENet, FPN); excluded where it is only ever a layer inside another model
column5: Excluding all components, or admitting all of them
column6: The line is `is it ever run on its own', which is weakly defined.
column7: Several corpus names (`cross attention', `slot attention', `film', `compositional attention') sit on this line.

column2: Kernel machines and Gaussian processes admitted though nonparametric
column4: Admitted: the learned object is the dual coefficients / kernel hyperparameters plus the retained points
column5: Excluded with k-NN as having no separable learned object
column6: k-NN learns nothing; an SVM learns coefficients and a GP learns hyperparameters. The retained data is part of the object, as the codebook is for VQ-VAE.
column7: If refused, the kernel-machine root collapses to kernel ridge regression.

column2: UL2, prefix-LMs, XLNet
column3: R4 (the Transformer division must be total)
column4: UL2 under Encoder-decoder (it is T5-derived); XLNet under Transformer-XL
column5: A fourth division value `prefix-LM'
column6: A fourth value would be field-named but would hold almost nothing; the two named cases are both resolvable by their lineage instead.
column7: If prefix-LMs proliferate, the division stops being total and a design pass must add the value.

column2: AdaBoost ensemble placed under boosted TREE ensembles
column4: Placed there: its canonical base learner is a stump
column5: A base-learner-agnostic `Boosted ensemble' node outside the Decision tree root
column6: A generic boosted-ensemble node would have no architecture of its own, which is what the admission rule asks for.
column7: AdaBoost over non-tree learners has no home.

column2: The second pass will meet names with no possible parent
column4: Declared policy: an unplaceable name is FLAGGED for a design pass, never given an invented parent and never promoted to a root by the second pass
column5: Letting the second pass create a root or a grouping node for it
column6: R7 exists to stop exactly that; v0's root set is what happens when it is allowed.
column7: Without an explicit flag channel in the second-pass tooling, R7 will be violated silently.
